hypothesis: H2: a reverse curriculum over start states (shoot from near goal -> dribble from midfield -> full game) reaches full-game mastery in fewer total env steps than whole-game practice; no synthetic rewards, only the start-state distribution changes.

tests.correction: holm-bonferroni over the 5-comparison primary family (MW and Welch families adjusted separately; registered decisions ride on the MW Holm p)

claims.claim: drills beat whole-game practice for epsilon-greedy learners: drills-varied reaches 90% full-game eval success in fewer total env steps than whole
claims.evidence: t90 IQM drills-varied=15125 vs whole=40375 steps; MW p_holm=3.93e-09, Welch p_holm=3.4e-09; censored drills-varied 0/30, whole 6/30.

claims.claim: the drill benefit is an exploration effect: it disappears or reverses when whole-game training starts from optimistic initialization (Q0=1.0)
claims.evidence: t90 IQM drills-varied=15125 vs whole-optimistic=16000 steps; MW p_holm=0.182, Welch p_holm=0.4; censored drills-varied 0/30, whole-optimistic 0/30. The drill advantage DISAPPEARS: no significant difference against optimistic whole-game training.

claims.claim: drill structure adds benefit beyond mere start-state diversity: drills-varied faster than uniform exploring starts over the same 40% of budget
claims.evidence: t90 IQM drills-varied=15125 vs explore-starts=43375 steps; MW p_holm=9.11e-11, Welch p_holm=4.85e-14; censored drills-varied 0/30, explore-starts 5/30.

conclusion.summary: Time to 90% eval success (IQM steps): whole=40375, drills-varied=15125, drills-fixed=21000, whole-optimistic=16000, explore-starts=43375. drills-varied vs whole: MW Holm p=3.93e-09, Welch Holm p=3.4e-09. Verdicts: claim 1 (drills beat whole) — supported; claim 2 (exploration boundary under optimistic init) — boundary; claim 3 (structure vs start diversity) — supported. Censored: whole 6/30, drills-varied 0/30, drills-fixed 0/30, whole-optimistic 0/30, explore-starts 5/30.
